c.tagline: The dusty Sahelian capital where the Chari and Logone rivers meet.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis rarely use meters; fares (often shared rides along fixed routes) are negotiated before departure, and private/full-taxi hire costs several times the shared rate.

emergency.note: Emergency response is very limited; the US Embassy recommends contacting SOS Médecins Tchad for medical evacuation coordination.

avoid.reason: Avoid the city outskirts and riverbanks after dark and the surroundings of the presidential palace and military sites, where photography is banned; foreign missions restrict staff to central districts.
Violent crime and carjacking risk mean no walking after dark, discreet valuables, and carrying ID for frequent police checkpoints.

hood_desc: The commercial and diplomatic core along Avenue Charles de Gaulle, home to N'Djamena's international-brand hotels, banks, embassies and the Grand Marché; best for business travelers and short stays who want walkable access to services and security presence.

A leafy, relatively affluent residential/diplomatic quarter along the Chari river with embassies and NGO compounds; suits longer-stay visitors, diplomats and aid workers wanting quieter surroundings close to the river.
A riverside district near the Chari and Chagoua market, mixing local guesthouses with everyday Chadian life; suits budget travelers and those wanting a more authentic, less touristy base.
A dense, lively residential and market neighborhood south of downtown known for its market and modest auberges; suits budget travelers comfortable with a working-class, bustling area.
An area near the airport with a mix of residential compounds and modest lodging; suits travelers with early/late flights or short layovers prioritizing airport proximity over central location.

water.note: Tap water is unsafe; use bottled or boiled water only.

sys.n: STAT (Société de Transport Automobile du Tchad) city buses

transit.pay: Fares on buses and shared taxis/minibuses are paid in cash directly to the driver or conductor in small XAF denominations; there is no electronic fare card system. Private taxi fares are agreed in cash before the ride.
transit.hours: Public transport generally operates roughly 6am-8pm; there is little to no organized night service, and travel after dark is typically by private/hired vehicle.
transit.note: Formal public transit is minimal and unreliable; most residents and visitors rely on shared or private taxis and moto-taxis.

bus: Intercity bush taxis/minibuses to regional towns
ferry: Small pirogue/ferry crossings of the Chari River to Cameroon (Kousseri)

tip.r: Not deeply ingrained but appreciated in hotels/restaurants catering to expats; rounding up or 5-10% is common at upscale establishments.
